indicators.note: into says the politician is set inside the jumbled word
clumsy suggests something done awkwardly, so the letters of lie are knocked out of order

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual politician

explanation.surface: A politician is accused of forcing a ham-fisted untruth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lie' looks like the untruth the politician tells, but its letters are only the jumbled fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone on by pressure is to compel them, a synonym of force as a verb.

parts.note: seems to be about the arts flourishing, but means warm containers in which bacterial cultures are grown

explanation.surface: Examples of how the arts and civilisation grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Laboratory cabinets keep microbial cultures warm so they grow, cases where cultures develop.

indicators.note: not says the word for an essay is removed from the word for verse

parts.note: verse is poetry
an essay is an attempt, a try

explanation.surface: An author of poems who never wrote prose pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essay' looks like a prose piece, but here it means an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan, the American author of tales and poems, is a writer.

parts.note: L stands for the pound, from the Latin libra, a unit of money
to make money is to earn it

explanation.surface: Someone finds that money breeds more money.
explanation.definitionFit: To find out something is to acquire knowledge of it, a synonym of discovers.

clue.text: All hard cases in this family

definitions.text: All hard cases in this family

parts.words: All hard cases in this family
parts.note: reads like tough criminals in one household, but means a zoological class whose members all wear hard shells

explanation.surface: Every one of the household is a tough nut.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabs, lobsters and shrimps belong to the class of shelled arthropods, whose bodies are cased in a hard crust.

clue.text: Problem afoot? Bill misplaced in sequence

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled name inside the word for sequence

parts.note: a sequence of linked things is a chain

indicators.note: misplaced means put in the wrong place, so the letters of Bill are disordered

explanation.surface: A man named Bill gets lost in a series of events, suggesting trouble brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'afoot' seems to mean under way; it is literal, a sore on the foot. 'misplaced' turns BILL into ILBL.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful itchy swelling caused by cold often affects the toes, so it is a foot complaint.

clue.text: Remove covering from a European fiddle

parts.note: un is the French word for a, so a European a
to fiddle is to rig, manipulate dishonestly

explanation.surface: A con involving someone from Europe strips something bare.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip a ship's rigging or tackle away is to take its covering gear off.

clue.text: Prepare to fight to obtain knight's insignia

parts.note: to obtain is to take
a knight's heraldic insignia are his arms, his coat of arms

explanation.surface: Getting a knight's emblem as he gets ready for battle.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pick up weapons and ready oneself for combat.

clue.text: Focus one's attention on money in box

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the word for box

parts.note: a box is a crate
taken as written
a cent is a small coin, money

explanation.surface: Concentrate your attention on the cash in the box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money in box' reads as cash stored away, but 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To direct one's mind fully on something is the verb sense meaning to focus.

indicators.note: in sets the word for work inside the symbol for silver

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a machine that works goes

explanation.surface: Someone keen to work with silver.
explanation.definitionFit: Being keenly excited and expectant is what eager means here.

parts.note: a knight called Maurice suggests a title, and the French singer Maurice ... bore the French word for knight as his surname

explanation.surface: A question about a knighted man named Maurice.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Chevalier was a French entertainer; his surname is French for a knight, hence 'Sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for a knight, addressed as Sir, is also the surname of the singer Maurice.

indicators.note: in places the word for terminating within the boxing abbreviation

parts.note: KO is the boxing abbreviation for knockout
to terminate is to end

explanation.surface: A bout of fighting is brought to a close with a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese martial art of sword fighting with bamboo staves is a form of combat.

clue.text: How one may be evicted, in all cases?

definitions.text: How one may be evicted, in all cases?

parts.words: How one may be evicted, in all cases?
parts.note: in all cases seems to mean always, but cases are luggage: an evicted tenant is thrown out with all their belongings

explanation.surface: A question about the manner in which tenants are thrown out, universally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means completely, with all one's belongings, as someone turned out of a home leaves.

clue.text: It was given to Maltese boatman on bridge

definitions.text: It was given to Maltese boatman on bridge

parts.words: It was given to Maltese boatman on bridge
parts.note: seems to describe a medal for one sailor; in fact the award was given to the whole island of Malta in 1942

explanation.surface: A Maltese sailor on the bridge received a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: King George VI awarded the bravery medal to the island of Malta collectively in 1942, so 'Maltese' covers every islander.
explanation.definitionFit: The British civilian gallantry medal was awarded to the island of Malta for its wartime endurance.

clue.text: Bugsy Malone production presenting no problems?

definitions.meaning: Bugsy Malone is a gangster musical whose roles are all played by youngsters, so its production is a play by kids
something presenting no difficulty is very easy

explanation.surface: Staging a kids' gangster musical turns out to be easy.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama performed by youngsters, and the idiom for a task that is very easy.

clue.text: Too many bad workmen tend to blame it

definitions.text: bad workmen tend to blame it

parts.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a crossword stand-in for many

explanation.surface: Lots of poor tradesmen are inclined to blame their equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says a bad workman blames his implements.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement used by a craftsman is what the proverb says a poor worker finds fault with.

parts.note: Paris is the French capital city
to copy something is to match it

explanation.surface: A city's duplicate is used for a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The French weekly news and photo publication is a well-known periodical.

clue.text: Bad temper the result of sick jokes?

parts.note: sick means ill
jokes are humour

explanation.surface: Bad temper comes from distasteful jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy, cross mood is what bad temper means.

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces read upward, backwards

parts.note: to issue is to emit
on means about, concerning
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Someone raises a point about volunteers and gets a firm refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raised' turns the whole run EMIT ON TA upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on no occasion whatever, the same as never.

parts.note: sounds like a district of rebels, but means a quarter of a full revolution, a ninety-degree turn

explanation.surface: A question about a district full of rebels.
explanation.definitionFit: A full turn is 360 degrees; a quarter of it is the ninety-degree corner of a square.

clue.text: Before conversion, his original character was different

definitions.text: Before conversion, his original character was different

parts.words: Before conversion, his original character was different
parts.note: seems to say a convert changed his personality, but means the apostle was called Saul before his conversion: only the first letter differed

explanation.surface: Before he found religion, this man was another person entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: Saul of Tarsus took a new name after his conversion on the road to Damascus; 'character' is a letter, S changing to P.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle was named Saul before his conversion, a name differing only in the initial letter.

parts.note: a harvest's yield is its crop
something increased is up

explanation.surface: A farmer hopes for a bigger harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to arise unexpectedly, to occur.

parts.note: stifling, airless weather is close
billets are soldiers' lodgings, quarters

explanation.surface: Soldiers find their airless lodgings too tight.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a confined, crowded space where people are packed tightly together.

clue.text: Delicate and charming female trapped by rising river

indicators.note: trapped by means the letter is enclosed inside the turned river
rising in a down clue means the river is read upward, backwards

parts.note: the Nile is the African river

explanation.surface: A dainty woman is caught as the river floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns NILE into ELIN, and F is put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Small, dainty and impish like a fairy, the adjective means delicate and charming.

parts.note: seems to describe a person determined to yield, but means a joint that flexes when one ... in submission

explanation.surface: A person intent on yielding.
explanation.definitionFit: The leg joint is the one that bends when someone kneels in homage.

clue.text: Biblical character producing no end of a minor riot

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new order
no end of says the final letter of the phrase is dropped

explanation.surface: A small disturbance from a youngster leads to a Biblical figure appearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of' takes the R from A MINOR, leaving AMINO, which 'riot' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth's mother-in-law in the Old Testament book of Ruth is a figure from scripture.

parts.note: seems to describe an oppressed factory hand, but means a lever literally trodden down to work a machine

explanation.surface: An oppressed factory hand is described.
explanation.definitionFit: A lever pressed by the sole operates a sewing machine or similar device, so it is literally stepped on.

definitions.meaning: a charge owed, as in membership ...

explanation.definitionFit: Fitting and proper as an adjective; as a noun, a charge or subscription owed.

indicators.note: on, in an across clue, here means the second piece follows after the word for each

parts.note: harsher, more severe, sterner

explanation.surface: Someone from the East is said to be rather harsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the East, the Orient, is a native of that region.

clue.text: Goodness is a major point in compassion

indicators.note: in sets the compass point inside the word for compassion

parts.note: compassion is pity
E, East, is one of the four cardinal or major compass points

explanation.surface: Virtue is said to lie chiefly in compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a major point' looks like an important argument; here it is a cardinal compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious devotion and virtue are what goodness means in this moral sense.
